Our war-time member, Etienne Gailly (Steve) and Belgium Olympic Marathon hero has been awarded the annual Grand Prix d'honneur for the outstanding athlete of the year 1948; and at Brussels he was awarded the annual "Trophie National du Merite Sportif," chosen on account of his Olympic Marathon performance.

In the 1948 Olympic Marathon E'tienne Gailly (Belgium) was first into Wembley Stadium only to stagger round and be passed by D. Cabrera (Argentine) and our old friend, Tom Richards of S.L.H.

On his return to Belgium he became one of the heroes of the 1948 Olympic Games. Étienne (Steve) Gailly was first into Wembley Stadium for the finish, but was so exhausted that Cabrera (Argentine) and Britain's own Tom Richards (S.L.H.) passed him on what must have seemed an endless lap of the track.

The grand finale, the Marathon, provided its usual high drama with Cabrera of Argentina catching Belgium's Etienne Gailly four hundred metres from the tape closely, followed by Britain's Tommy Richards, who had run a very sensible race.

Etienne Gailly, the Belgian who so very nearly won the 1948 Olympic Marathon was also one of the Belgrave group. When peace arrived in 1945 Charlie Smart went to Germany with the Control Commission where he was unbeaten over 5,000/10,000 metres for two years and was the U.K.'s second ranked 6 miler.
Second Lieutenant Gailly played his part and before too long was reunited with his family, although still managing to get back to see his running friends in England.
